body.statement: There is a class-uniform constant \(C\) such that, after an optimizing group permutation and the coordinate baseline gauges, \(\mathcal E(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\le C D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\) for all \(\theta,\widetilde\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\).
body.justification: It converts the statistical law metric into the exact analytic defects that can control the density quotient and its incompressible kernel.
body.gap: Khesin et al. identify Hellinger geometry only on the density quotient; the intervention-ratio terms needed to control the quotient fiber are absent there.
body.consumer: Every population and finite-sample recovery statement can work with observable Hellinger error rather than unobservable score identities.
